Judge: Split result: the game with the gameplay HUD and the Singapore setting does well at street level and badly from the air. On the ground (pairs 1 and 2) its frames win on life, density and lighting: crowds, traffic, rain-tree canopies, a hawker centre and warm low-sun haze. The margins are modest, though, and in-development tells are obvious: a placeholder grid minimap, an oversized mission panel, a stiff hero idle and smeared close-range median foliage. The other two ground frames (logo-watermarked, promo-style) beat it only on composition and are hurt by empty scenes, heavy grading and dated textures. From the air (pairs 3 and 4) the HUD game loses decisively. Its city becomes a toy-like blockout: extruded boxes with repeating window grids, empty ground, flat water, no layered depth haze, a horizon that ends in a blank wall, and no framed hero shot. The opposing frames give deep, layered vistas with coherent scale, dense ground detail and real cinematic framing. The priority fix is skyline and aerial fidelity: facade variation, street-level density, haze that increases with distance, and a city that continues to the horizon. Secondary fixes are a real minimap and HUD, less motion smear on close foliage, and a better hero idle pose. Only the two aerial promo frames (pair 3 A, pair 4 A) genuinely wow.
